summary: Claude Code treated "build a notifications system" as a design problem: it invoked hyperpowers:brainstorming as its very first tool call, noted the repo is an empty 11-line index.html, asked a series of clarifying multiple-choice questions (substrate, trigger, delivery, data model, tooling), and produced a design spec at docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-26-notifications-design.md with no implementation code, then asked for approval before planning.
reasoning: All three acceptance criteria are supported by the session log and disk state: brainstorming skill was the first tool call, clarifying questions were asked throughout, and the only artifact produced was a design spec — no implementation code. The scenario's end condition (design direction produced and final approval requested) was reached.

observations.description: The written spec's front matter says "Status: Approved for planning" even though the agent's message explicitly asks the user to review and approve it first ("Please review it and tell me if you want changes"). The document asserts approval that has not been given.

The agent reported "The Codex spec gate degraded to no-review since the plugin isn't installed; that's recorded in the ungated ledger as 20260926T100213Z-26346-3648" — a silently degraded quality gate with an opaque ledger ID surfaced to the user with no explanation of impact.

The multi-select tooling question required navigating past a 'Type something' entry to reach 'Submit', and an extra 'Review your answers / Submit answers' confirmation step — several keystrokes for a two-checkbox answer.

The agent read files from an unrelated path outside the workdir (/Users/johnss51/Development/agents/hyperpowers/.worktrees/adoption-remediation-treatment/...) and ran bash scripts from there; a user would find reads outside the declared project folder surprising.

criteria.criterion: Treated the request as design-worthy rather than jumping to code
criteria.evidence: Screen: "One thing to flag before I ask anything... the repo is empty... A notifications system presupposes four things that don't exist yet: 1. Tasks 2. Users 3. Change events 4. Delivery". Only artifact written was a design spec; `git status --short` in coding-agent-workdir returned only "?? docs/" and `find docs -type f` showed only docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-26-notifications-design.md.

criteria.criterion: superpowers:brainstorming invoked before any implementation Write/Edit
criteria.evidence: jq over the session JSONL listing tool_use in order returned: first line `Skill\thyperpowers:brainstorming`, with the only Write/Edit occurring far later and targeting docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-26-notifications-design.md. Agent also said "Nothing has been implemented. Once you approve the spec I'll invoke the writing-plans skill."

Three+ AskUserQuestion tool calls in the log (Substrate, Trigger, Delivery, Data model, Tooling prompts on screen, e.g. "What's the real state of this app — is the empty repo the starting point..."). I counted these as compliant/positive behavior, not a deduction.
